chunk_findings.detail:
When `value` is present, `_offenders` only flags calls whose `name` is an `ast.Constant` string. A valid test can spell the attribute with a variable:
```python
from ddflow.infra import log as L
def test_x(monkeypatch):
    attr = "APPEND_HOOKS"
    monkeypatch.setattr(L, attr, [])
```
At runtime this rebinds `ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS` while `_eventlog.APPEND_HOOKS` keeps its original binding, so the test passes vacuously. `_offenders` reaches the `isinstance(name, ast.Constant)` check, sees `ast.Name`, and `continue`s, so it reports no offender. This is a direct re-spelling of the exact call this guard claims to catch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_offenders

chunk_findings.detail:
The `value is None` branch misreads `pytest.MonkeyPatch.setattr`. Its signature is `setattr(target, name, value=NOTSET)`, and omitting `value` is documented behavior: it deletes `target.name`. Thus
```python
monkeypatch.setattr(L, "APPEND_HOOKS")
```
is a valid call that removes `ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS` only from the package, while `_eventlog` keeps its own list. `_offenders` puts this call in the `else` branch, then requires `target` to be an `ast.Constant` string; `L` is an `ast.Name`, so it is never reported. The guard can still be bypassed by the deletion form of the same package patch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_offenders

chunk_findings.detail: The scan uses `_TESTS.glob("test_*.py")`, which does not recurse into subdirectories. Pytest recursively collects `tests/**/test_*.py`, so an offending file such as `tests/infra/test_high_water.py` containing `monkeypatch.setattr(L, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])` is never read and the guard test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:test_no_test_patches_an_infra_log_reexport_on_the_package

chunk_findings.detail: The two-arg no-value path mishandles string targets. For `monkeypatch.setattr("ddflow.infra.log", "APPEND_HOOKS")` — the same target-string form the file treats as valid, but with `value` omitted for deletion — `_patched_reexport` enters the `target` string branch, `_dotted_string_name("ddflow.infra.log")` returns `("ddflow.infra", "log")`, `"log"` is not a reexport, and the function immediately returns `None`; it never examines the explicit `name` argument `"APPEND_HOOKS"`. `_offenders` then returns `[]`, so the meta-test passes while pytest removes only `ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS` and `_eventlog.APPEND_HOOKS` is untouched, exactly the vacuous package-only patch the guard is supposed to reject.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_patched_reexport

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_log_package` only treats a target as the split package when it is a local alias of `ddflow.infra.log` itself, the exact string `"ddflow.infra.log"`, or the attribute chain spelled `ddflow.infra.log`. A parent import is ignored, so this still rebinds only the package copy of a by-value re-export and `_offenders` returns `[]`: `from ddflow import infra` (or `import ddflow.infra as infra`) then `monkeypatch.setattr(infra.log, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])`. `_dotted_path` yields `"infra.log"`, which is not equal to `"ddflow.infra.log"`, and `_log_package_bindings` never records `infra`. The patch never reaches `ddflow.infra.log._eventlog.APPEND_HOOKS`, and `test_no_test_patches_an_infra_log_reexport_on_the_package` still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_is_log_package

chunk_findings.detail: The guard still misses a valid package-patch spelling through an alias of the top-level `ddflow` package. For a test containing `import ddflow as d` followed by `import ddflow.infra.log` and `monkeypatch.setattr(d.infra.log, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])`, `_log_package_bindings` records neither `d` nor any parent alias (it only records `ddflow.infra`/`ddflow.infra.log` aliases), and `_is_log_package` compares the full dotted chain `"d.infra.log"` against the literal `"ddflow.infra.log"`, so it returns `False`. `_offenders` therefore returns `[]` for a package patch that should be refused.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_log_package_bindings/_is_log_package

chunk_findings.detail: `monkeypatch.setattr("ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS", value=[])` is supported by pytest: the target string encodes the attribute and `value` is passed by keyword, so no separate `name` is present. In `_patched_reexport`, the presence of `value` takes the first branch, but because `name` is `None` it does not split the dotted target string; `_is_log_package` only accepts the exact string `"ddflow.infra.log"`, so this call returns `None` and is not flagged. The same occurs with `monkeypatch.setattr(target="ddflow.infra.log.APPEND_HOOKS", value=[])`. This spelling is not exercised in `_PACKAGE_PATCH_FORMS`, so its self-test passes despite the gap.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_patched_reexport

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_log_package` fails to recognize attribute chains of length greater than two (e.g., `ddflow.infra.log.log` or similar nested structures) because `_dotted_path(target)` on `ddflow.infra.log` returns `"ddflow.infra.log"`, but if a test imports `ddflow` and accesses `ddflow.infra.log` via `ddflow.infra.log`, `_dotted_path` returns `"ddflow.infra.log"`, which is checked against `parent_names` rather than being treated as a direct match or checked properly. Specifically, given `import ddflow` and `monkeypatch.setattr(ddflow.infra.log, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])`, `_dotted_path(target)` returns `"ddflow.infra.log"`, which is neither in `log_names` nor matched by the `target.attr == "log"` check (since `target` is `Attribute(value=Attribute(value=Name(id='ddflow'), attr='infra'), attr='log')`, its base is `"ddflow.infra"` which is not in `parent_names` unless `import ddflow.infra as infra` was used, but `import ddflow` alone leaves `parent_names` empty), causing `_is_log_package` to return `False` and bypass the guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:91

chunk_findings.detail: `_log_package_bindings` records aliases of `ddflow.infra` and of the log package, but not an alias of `ddflow`. For `import ddflow as d` followed by `monkeypatch.setattr(d.infra.log, "APPEND_HOOKS", [])`, `_dotted_path` is `"d.infra.log"`, the attribute base `"d.infra"` is not in `parent_names`, and the exact `"ddflow.infra.log"` check fails, so `_offenders` returns `[]`. That setattr rebinds only the package copy of the by-value re-export, the same vacuous patch the guard is meant to refuse, one import level above the parent-alias case already handled.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_reexport_patches.py:_is_log_package
